findings.disposition_note: the repair belongs with the figure producer scripts/prototypes/diiid_edge_current_refusal/render.py, where the star is plotted after the refused marks at a higher zorder
findings.summary: The source-cutoff star is drawn at zorder 15 directly over one of the refused-proposal circles, which is drawn at zorder 14 with a smaller marker, so the right panel shows four circles while its own footer reports '5 cells change in terminal refused proposals'. The star's single crossing cell (R, Z) = (1.212, 0.800) m is exactly one of the five refused cells (cutoff-jumps.json smallest_crossing_pair.crossing_rz_m equals a spatial.json terminal refused changed_rz_m to floating-point identity). Measured from the PNG, four of the five refused coordinates map to visible circles at (974, 320), (1124, 320), (1041, 519) and (974, 434) px, and the fifth maps to the star's centre at (989, 264) px within 1 px. A reader reconciling the reported count with the picture sees four marks and cannot tell that a fifth refused cell exists.

Same defect in this row: the single source-cutoff crossing cell coincides exactly with one of the nine refused cells (checked cell by cell against spatial.json), so the right panel shows eight countable circles against a footer reporting nine refused cells.

Same defect in this row: the source-cutoff cell coincides exactly with one of the 43 refused cells, so one of the 43 refused marks is drawn as a star instead of a circle and the countable marks do not reconcile with the footer.

findings.disposition_note: render.py legend handles at lines 255-264 and 286-293
findings.summary: The legend gives 'mask change' and 'EFIT null' the same hollow-square glyph and differs only in colour, so the key cannot teach a shape distinction. Measured in the rendered PNG, the mask-change swatch at (415, 47) and the EFIT-null swatch at (976, 22) are both plain 14x14 hollow squares; in the plot the two marks also share the square marker and differ only by size and grey/near-black. On the dense panels a reader must infer which hollow squares are changed support cells and which are solution nulls from position and colour alone.

The mask-change marks are drawn at ms=4 with a 0.8 pt edge at zorder 1, under the contours and the wall. In frame-146-limited the 347 cells pack into a grey lattice that is the heaviest ink in the panel, while the flux topology the panel exists to show is a set of thin lines beneath it; the mark that encodes the count outweighs the mark that encodes the physics.

Both poloidal panels are 14 in wide with equal-aspect limits of R 0.75-2.65 m against Z -1.7-1.7 m, so each panel fills about 270 px of the 1400 px canvas and more than half the figure is white margin; the contour topology is drawn at roughly a third of the width the canvas offers, which is a legibility loss on the page the figure is read on.

findings.disposition_note: render.py legend line 264 and footer lines 308-315
findings.summary: The footer counts the grey square as 'support cells' ('2 support cells; 0 shadow nodes change') while the legend names the same mark 'mask change', so a reader cannot tell whether the footer's count refers to the grey squares or to something that is not drawn. The two names for one mark appear within the same figure.

findings.disposition_note: the repair is the same mark-density decision in render.py
findings.summary: 96 refused-proposal circles at ms=6 overlap one another into a continuous red band across the inboard half of the right panel, and the flux contours beneath that band cannot be traced through it. The band is denser than the 43-circle chain in frame-179-limited and is the dominant mark in a figure whose purpose is to show the retained footprint.

findings.disposition_note: the identity is the recorded result of the paired reference arm, not a rendering defect, and the caption in the evidence fragment is the right place for it
findings.summary: This attachment is byte-identical to the frame-146-limited attachment, so the nine-figure evidence set contains one picture under two names. The duplication is the reference arm deliberately reproducing the unmodified 146L row and the run's own figure-inspections record notes the shared SHA; a reader browsing the figures index has only the caption to tell them it is not a second measurement.

In the 146-limited inactive-field panel the highest labelled tick is 24 mT while the largest spikes rise above it, so the biggest excursion has no labelled value and must be interpolated against an unlabelled stretch of the vertical axis.

findings.disposition_note: a shared key for two rows of the same colours is the conventional form here, and splitting it would duplicate a legend across four columns
findings.summary: The legend joins two rows into one entry ('live residual / returned support', 'frozen residual / incoming support') and both rows use the same blue, so the reader has to infer from the row titles which half of each label applies above and which below. Nothing is unreadable, but the key requires a decoding step the panels do not make explicit.

summary: All nine attached PNGs were opened and judged. Four of the nine pass every rubric item without a defect worth recording. One blocking defect recurs in three poloidal panels: the source-cutoff star is plotted over a refused-proposal circle at exactly the same cell, so the panel shows one fewer refused mark than its own footer reports. The remaining findings are non-blocking: a legend that gives two different marks the same square, a changed-cell lattice that outweighs the contours, a two-panel layout that leaves more than half the canvas blank, a footer and legend that name one mark differently, an overlapping refused band in the suppressed panel, an unlabelled peak above the highest tick in the 146-limited field panel, a joined legend key in the trip traces, and one attachment that is byte-identical to another.
